        i.giftvalusd,
        i.gifttot,
        (i.giftvalusd * i.gifttot / 100.0) AS gift_impact_quotient,
        ms.spendusd,
        ms.membkind
    FROM fans f
    JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
)
SELECT 
    userregistry,
    nicklabel,
    ROUND(gift_impact_quotient, 2) AS giq,
    membkind
FROM gift_metrics
WHERE 
    gift_impact_quotient > 50
    AND spendusd < 100
    AND membkind IN ('Free', 'Basic')
ORDER BY gift_impact_quotient DESC;

question: Can you recognize all Whale fans in our system? I need a list showing their user ID, nickname, and total financial support in USD (combining both direct spending and gift values). Sort the results by total support amount from highest to lowest. Need to consider all fans who may not have interaction records in our system yet.
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Identify high-spending "whale" fans who provide extraordinary financial support
Knowledge used: [27] Whale
Advanced PSQL features: Date filtering, COALESCE function
*/

SELECT 
    f.userregistry,
    f.nicklabel,
    (ms.spendusd + COALESCE(i.giftvalusd, 0)) AS total_support_usd
FROM 
    fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    LEFT JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry
WHERE 
    (COALESCE(i.giftvalusd, 0) > 500 OR ms.spendusd > 1000)
    AND (i.timemark IS NULL OR i.timemark > CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days')
ORDER BY 
    total_support_usd DESC;

question: Show me a breakdown of our fan base using the tierstep classification system. I need to see each tier category, the count of fans in each category, their average points, and average spending amounts. All the calculations should be rounded to 2 decimal places. Include all fans with Active or VIP status, and make sure to include data from fans who may not have spending records in our system yet.
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Analyze fans based on their tier progression and status
Knowledge used: [1] tierstep
Advanced PSQL features: CASE expressions, Conditional grouping
*/

-- Step 1: Group fans by tier levels and analyze distribution
WITH tiered_fans AS (
    SELECT 
        CASE
            WHEN f.tierstep BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN 'Entry-level'
            WHEN f.tierstep BETWEEN 4 AND 7 THEN 'Mid-level'
            WHEN f.tierstep BETWEEN 8 AND 10 THEN 'High-level'
            WHEN f.tierstep > 10 THEN 'Core'
            ELSE 'Undefined'
        END AS tier_category,
        f.ptsval,
        COALESCE(ms.spendusd, 0) AS spendusd
    FROM 
        fans f
        LEFT JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    WHERE 
        f.statustag IN ('Active', 'VIP')
)
SELECT 
    tier_category,
    COUNT(*) AS fan_count,
    ROUND(AVG(ptsval), 2) AS avg_points,
    ROUND(AVG(spendusd), 2) AS avg_spending
FROM tiered_fans
GROUP BY 1;

question: Please identify users who qualify as Content Creator Classification by showing their user ID, nickname, content quality score, content volume, follower count, and Content Creator Classification. Could you sort the results by content quality first, then by follower count - both in descending order?
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Find fans who create high-quality content for the platform
Knowledge used: [50]
Advanced PSQL features: JSONB path extraction, Conditional filtering
*/

-- Step 1: Extract content quality metrics and identify high-value creators
SELECT 
    f.userregistry,
    f.nicklabel,
    (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'contqualrate')::numeric AS content_quality,
    (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'ugcval')::int AS content_volume,
    (sc.community_engagement->'network'->>'follcount')::int AS follower_count,
    CASE
        WHEN (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'contqualrate')::numeric > 8.5
         AND (sc.community_engagement->'network'->>'follcount')::int > 1000
         AND (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'ugcval')::int > 20
        THEN 'High-Value Content Creator'
        WHEN (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'contqualrate')::numeric > 7.0
         AND (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'ugcval')::int > 20
        THEN 'Content Creator'
        ELSE 'Regular Fan'
    END AS creator_classification
FROM 
    fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg
    JOIN socialcommunity sc ON sc.socialengagepivot = e.engagereg
WHERE 
    (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'contqualrate')::numeric IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 
    content_quality DESC, follower_count DESC;

question: I'm trying to analyze the economic value of Silent Supporters on our platform. Show me these financially valuable users with their nicknames, Monetization Value, engagement rates, and chat-to-session ratios. Also include their membership tier, revenue generated per hour of viewing (by dividing their spending by watch hours), and their Content Preference Classification. Make sure to include all users who meet the Silent Supporter criteria, even if they're missing some interaction. Present the results in descending order by monetization value.
gold_sql:
/* 
Intent: Analyze the economic impact of silent supporters to optimize retention strategies
Knowledge used: [24] Silent Supporter, [51]
Advanced PSQL features: JSONB operators, Date ranges, Conditional filtering
*/

-- Step 1: Identify silent supporters based on Knowledge [24]
WITH fan_memberships AS (
    SELECT 
        f.userregistry,
        f.nicklabel,
        ms.memberreg,
        ms.spendusd,
        ms.membdays,
        ms.membkind
    FROM fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
),
fan_interactions AS (
    SELECT
        i.interactfanpivot AS userregistry,
        i.gifttot,
        (i.engagement_metrics->'chat_activity'->>'chatmsg')::int AS chatmsg,
        (i.engagement_metrics->'session'->>'watchhrs')::numeric AS watch_hours
    FROM interactions i
),
silent_supporters AS (
    SELECT 
        fm.userregistry,
        fm.nicklabel,
        fm.spendusd * (1 + fm.membdays/365.0 * 0.5) * (1 + COALESCE(fi.gifttot, 0)/10.0 * 0.2) AS mv,
        e.engrate,
        fi.chatmsg,
        p.sesscount,
        COALESCE(fi.chatmsg, 0)::float / NULLIF(p.sesscount, 0) AS chat_message_ratio,
        e.contpref,
        fm.membkind,
        fm.membdays,
        fm.spendusd,
        fi.watch_hours
    FROM fan_memberships fm
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = fm.memberreg
    LEFT JOIN fan_interactions fi ON fi.userregistry = fm.userregistry
    JOIN preferencesandsettings p ON p.preferencesmemberpivot = fm.memberreg
    WHERE 
        fm.spendusd * (1 + fm.membdays/365.0 * 0.5) * (1 + COALESCE(fi.gifttot, 0)/10.0 * 0.2) > 100 -- High MV
        AND e.engrate < 0.3 -- Low engagement
        AND COALESCE(fi.chatmsg, 0)::float / NULLIF(p.sesscount, 0) < 0.5 -- Low chat-to-session ratio
)
-- Step 2: Analyze their economic impact and viewing patterns
SELECT 
    nicklabel,
    mv,
    engrate,
    chat_message_ratio,
    membkind,
    spendusd / NULLIF(watch_hours, 0) AS revenue_per_hour,
    CASE
        WHEN contpref = 'Music' THEN 'Content Consumer (Music)'
        WHEN contpref = 'Dance' THEN 'Content Consumer (Dance)'
        WHEN contpref = 'Gaming' THEN 'Content Consumer (Gaming)'
        ELSE 'General Content Consumer'
    END AS viewer_category
FROM silent_supporters
ORDER BY mv DESC;

question: Give me a breakdown of fans by their churn risk level, showing the count of fans in each category, the average days since their last login, their average engagement rates, average interaction consistency, and a calculated average Retention Risk Factor for each group. All the calculations should be rounded to 2 decimal places. This will help me prioritize our retention strategies for different risk segments.
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Analyze fans based on churn risk levels and recency of activity
Knowledge used: [13] Retention Risk Factor, [52]
Advanced PSQL features: Date functions, CASE expressions, ROUND function
*/

-- Step 1: Group fans by churn risk level and calculate key metrics
SELECT 
    r.churnflag,
    COUNT(*) AS fan_count,
    ROUND(AVG(CURRENT_DATE - p.lastlogdt)::numeric, 2) AS avg_days_since_login,
    ROUND(AVG(e.engrate)::numeric, 2) AS avg_engagement_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(p.intconsist)::numeric, 2) AS avg_interaction_consistency,
    -- Basic RRF approximation for each group
    ROUND(AVG(
        (1 - p.intconsist) * 2 + 
        (CURRENT_DATE - p.lastlogdt)/30.0 * 0.5 + 
        CASE
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'None' THEN 0
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'Low' THEN 1
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'Medium' THEN 2
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'High' THEN 3
        END
    )::numeric, 2) AS avg_retention_risk_factor
FROM 
    fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg
    JOIN retentionandinfluence r ON r.retainengagepivot = e.engagereg
    JOIN preferencesandsettings p ON p.preferencesmemberpivot = ms.memberreg
GROUP BY 
    r.churnflag;

question: Provide me with each fan's id, nickname, their calculated FLV value (rounded to 2 decimals), and classify them based on Fan Value Segmentation. Please sort the results by FLV in descending order.
gold_sql:
/* 
Intent: Segment fans based on their lifetime value to prioritize marketing efforts
Knowledge used: [16] Fan Lifetime Value, [11] Monetization Value, [10] Fan Engagement Index, [53], [52]
Advanced PSQL features: CTEs, Percentile calculation, Case expressions
*/

-- Step 1: Calculate FEI components based on Knowledge [10]
WITH fan_memberships AS (
    SELECT 
        f.userregistry,
        f.nicklabel,
        ms.memberreg,
        ms.spendusd,
        ms.membdays,
        COALESCE(i.gifttot, 0) AS gifttot
    FROM fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    LEFT JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry
),
fan_engagement AS (
    SELECT 
        fm.userregistry,
        fm.nicklabel,
        e.engrate * 0.4 + 
        e.socintscore / 100 * 0.3 + 
        e.actdayswk / 7.0 * 0.2 + 
        e.avgsesscount / 10.0 * 0.1 AS fei,
        -- Calculate MV based on Knowledge [11]
        fm.spendusd * (1 + fm.membdays / 365.0 * 0.5) * 
        (1 + fm.gifttot / 10.0 * 0.2) AS mv,
        e.engagereg
    FROM fan_memberships fm
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = fm.memberreg
),
-- Step 3: Get retention risk using proper table relations
retention_risk AS (
    SELECT 
        fe.userregistry,
        fe.nicklabel,
        fe.fei,
        fe.mv,
        CASE 
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'None' THEN 0
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'Low' THEN 1
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'Medium' THEN 2
            WHEN r.churnflag = 'High' THEN 3
        END AS rrf_approx
    FROM fan_engagement fe
    JOIN retentionandinfluence r ON r.retainengagepivot = fe.engagereg
),
-- Step 4: Calculate FLV using Knowledge [16]
fan_lifetime_value AS (
    SELECT 
        userregistry,
        nicklabel,
        mv * (1 - rrf_approx / 10.0) * (1 + fei) * 24 AS flv
    FROM retention_risk
),
-- Step 5: Calculate percentile thresholds for segmentation
percentile_values AS (
    SELECT
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY flv) AS median,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY flv) AS p75,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY flv) AS p90
    FROM fan_lifetime_value
)
-- Step 6: Segment fans based on calculated percentiles
SELECT 
    f.userregistry,
    f.nicklabel,
    ROUND(f.flv, 2) AS flv,
    CASE 
        WHEN f.flv > p.p90 THEN 'Top Tier'
        WHEN f.flv > p.p75 THEN 'High Value'
        WHEN f.flv > p.median THEN 'Medium Value'
        ELSE 'Low Value'
    END AS value_segment
FROM fan_lifetime_value f, percentile_values p
ORDER BY f.flv DESC;

question: I need to identify our Community Pillars for upcoming platform development discussions. Show me a list of our community leaders with their nicknames, calculated Community Contribution Index scores rounded to two decimal places, their group roles, activity frequency, and membership duration in days. Only include fans who meet all the Community Pillar criteria. Sort the results by CCI score in descending order.
gold_sql:
/* 
Intent: Identify community pillars who should be included in platform development discussions
Knowledge used: [25] Community Pillar, [17] Community Contribution Index, [10], [14], [12]
Advanced PSQL features: JSON path navigation, Multiple condition JOINs, Array functions
*/

-- Step 1: Build foundation with fan membership data
WITH fan_memberships AS (
    SELECT 
        f.userregistry,
        f.nicklabel,
        ms.memberreg,
        ms.membdays
    FROM fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
),
-- Step 2: Gather engagement metrics with proper table relations
fan_engagement AS (
    SELECT 
        fm.userregistry,
        fm.nicklabel,
        fm.membdays,
        e.engagereg,
        e.engrate,
        e.socintscore,
        e.actdayswk,
        e.avgsesscount,
        e.actfreq,
        -- FEI approximation based on Knowledge [10]
        e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore / 100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk / 7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount / 10.0 * 0.1 AS fei_approx
    FROM fan_memberships fm
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = fm.memberreg
),
-- Step 3: Add social community data through correct relationship paths
community_data AS (
    SELECT 
        fe.userregistry,
        fe.nicklabel,
        fe.membdays,
        fe.actfreq,
        fe.fei_approx,
        sc.collabcount,
        sc.community_engagement,
        (sc.community_engagement->'group_involvement'->>'grprole')::text AS group_role,
        -- Get data for CCIS calculation
        (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'contqualrate')::numeric AS contqualrate,
        (sc.community_engagement->'content_creation'->>'ugcval')::numeric AS ugcval,
        (sc.community_engagement->'network'->>'follcount')::numeric AS follcount,
        -- Join to retention data for viral content count
        ri.viralcont
    FROM fan_engagement fe
    JOIN socialcommunity sc ON sc.socialengagepivot = fe.engagereg
    JOIN retentionandinfluence ri ON ri.retainengagepivot = fe.engagereg
),
-- Step 4: Calculate CCI components based on Knowledge [17]
cci_components AS (
    SELECT 
        cd.userregistry,
        cd.nicklabel,
        -- CCIS calculation based on Knowledge [12]
        cd.contqualrate * (cd.ugcval / 10.0) * (1 + cd.follcount / 100 * 0.5) AS ccis_approx,
        -- SIM calculation based on Knowledge [14]
        (cd.follcount / 100) * (fe.engrate * 2) * (COALESCE(cd.viralcont, 0) + 1) * 0.5 AS sim_approx,
        cd.collabcount,
        cd.fei_approx,
        cd.actfreq,
        cd.membdays,
        cd.group_role
    FROM community_data cd
    JOIN fan_engagement fe ON fe.userregistry = cd.userregistry
)
-- Step 5: Identify Community Pillars based on Knowledge [25]
SELECT 
    nicklabel,
    ROUND((ccis_approx * 0.4 + sim_approx * 0.3 + collabcount * 0.1 + fei_approx * 0.2)::numeric, 2) AS cci,
    group_role,
    actfreq,
    membdays
FROM cci_components
WHERE 
    (ccis_approx * 0.4 + sim_approx * 0.3 + collabcount * 0.1 + fei_approx * 0.2) > 7
    AND actfreq = 'Daily'
    AND membdays > 180
    AND (group_role = 'Moderator' OR group_role = 'Leader')
ORDER BY cci DESC;

question: Show me a list of fans with their user ID, nicknames, how many different idols they support, the names of these idols in array, and their average engagement rate rounded to 2 decimal places. Only include fans who are classified as Multi-Idol Supporters. Sort the results first by the number of idols supported (highest first), then by engagement rate (highest first).
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Identify fans who support multiple virtual idols
Knowledge used: [29] Multi-Idol Supporter
Advanced PSQL features: COUNT DISTINCT, GROUP BY, HAVING clause, ARRAY_AGG, ROUND function
*/

-- Step 1: Join fans to interactions directly, and establish correct path to engagement data
SELECT 
    f.userregistry,
    f.nicklabel,
    COUNT(DISTINCT i.interactidolpivot) AS idols_supported,
    ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT vi.nametag) AS idol_names,
    ROUND(AVG(e.engrate)::numeric, 2) AS avg_engagement_rate
FROM 
    fans f
    JOIN interactions i ON i.interactfanpivot = f.userregistry
    JOIN virtualidols vi ON vi.entityreg = i.interactidolpivot
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg
WHERE

GROUP BY

HAVING

ORDER BY

question: Find all Superfans in our database and display their nicknames, tier levels, Fan Engagement Index, and Monetization Value. Indicate which ones qualify as true Superfans based on the Superfan criteria and label them as 'Superfan', otherwise label them as 'Regular Fan'. Please sort the results by highest engagement first, then by monetary value in descending order. Only consider fans with active and VIP status.
gold_sql:
/* 
Intent: Identify fans who meet the criteria for Superfans
Knowledge used: [20] Superfan
Advanced PSQL features: CASE expression, Simple JOIN
*/

-- Step 1: Calculate approximation of Fan Engagement Index (FEI) components
SELECT 
    f.nicklabel,
    f.tierstep,
    ROUND((e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore/100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk/7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount/10.0 * 0.1)::numeric, 2) AS fei,
    ROUND((ms.spendusd * (1 + ms.membdays/365.0 * 0.5))::numeric, 2) AS mv,
    -- Flag as Superfan according to Knowledge [20]
    CASE
        WHEN f.tierstep >= 8 
         AND (e.engrate * 0.4 + e.socintscore/100 * 0.3 + e.actdayswk/7.0 * 0.2 + e.avgsesscount/10.0 * 0.1) > 0.7
         AND ms.spendusd * (1 + ms.membdays/365.0 * 0.5) > 200
        THEN 'Superfan'
        ELSE 'Regular Fan'
    END AS fan_classification
FROM 
    fans f
    JOIN membershipandspending ms ON ms.memberfanpivot = f.userregistry
    JOIN engagement e ON e.engagememberpivot = ms.memberreg
WHERE 
    f.statustag = 'Active' OR f.statustag = 'VIP'

question: Create a report evaluating observatory conditions using the Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI) and identifying stations meeting Optimal Observing Window (OOW) criteria. The output should group stations by whether meets OOW (bool:True or False). For each group, you should provide its boolean value of OOW, the count of stations, average AOI (rounded to 3 decimal places) and a JSON array whose elements each include  `station` (observatory name), `aoi` (AOI value), `lunar_factors` object with `stage` (lunar stage) and `distance` (lunar distance), and `solar_status` (solar status).
gold_sql:
-- This query evaluates optimal observatory conditions using Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI)
-- and generates a JSON report of environmental factors using JSON aggregation functions.
-- Using KB knowledge: Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI) [id: 1], Optimal Observing Window (OOW) [id: 13]

-- Step 1: Calculate AOI for each observatory and determine if conditions meet Optimal Observing Window criteria
WITH observatory_conditions AS (
    SELECT 
        o.ObservStation,
        o.AtmosTransparency * (1 - o.HumidityRate/100) * (1 - 0.02 * o.WindSpeedMs) AS aoi,  -- AOI formula from KB
        o.LunarStage,
        o.LunarDistDeg,
        o.SolarStatus,
        -- Check if conditions meet OOW criteria
        CASE WHEN 
            o.AtmosTransparency * (1 - o.HumidityRate/100) * (1 - 0.02 * o.WindSpeedMs) > 0.85 AND
            (o.LunarStage = 'New' OR o.LunarStage = 'First Quarter') AND
            o.LunarDistDeg > 45 AND
            (o.SolarStatus = 'Low' OR o.SolarStatus = 'Moderate')
        THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_optimal_window
    FROM 
        Observatories o
)
-- Step 2: Generate JSON report grouping observatories by optimal condition status
SELECT 
    is_optimal_window,
    COUNT(*) AS station_count,
    ROUND(AVG(aoi)::numeric, 3) AS avg_aoi,
    -- Use JSON aggregation to create detailed environmental factors report
    jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'station', ObservStation,
        'aoi', ROUND(aoi::numeric, 3),
        'lunar_factors', jsonb_build_object(
            'stage', LunarStage,
            'distance', LunarDistDeg
        ),
        'solar_status', SolarStatus
    )) AS observatory_details
FROM 
    observatory_conditions
GROUP BY 
    is_optimal_window;

question: Would you generate a comprehensive report categorizing sites based on High Fidelity Mesh standard? For each archaeological location, please include the site code, side name, total mesh count, high-fidelity mesh count and proportion (as a percentage), the average Mesh Complexity Ratio, average resolution parameters (in mm), average geometric accuracy measurements and Mesh Quality Classification. The data should be presented in descending order of high-fidelity percentage.
gold_sql:
/*
 * SQL Intent: Identify sites with High Fidelity Meshes and analyze mesh quality distribution
 * Knowledge Used: #13 (High Fidelity Mesh), #4 (Mesh Complexity Ratio - MCR) #53
 * Advanced Functions: CASE expressions, Window functions (RANK()), String functions
 */

WITH mesh_analysis AS (
    -- Step 1: Calculate Mesh Complexity Ratio (MCR) and identify High Fidelity Meshes
    SELECT 
        sm.zoneref AS site_code,
        sm.facetregistry AS mesh_id,
        -- Calculate MCR based on Knowledge #4
        (sm.facetfaces / (sm.facetverts * POWER(sm.facetresmm, 2))) * 1000 AS mcr,
        sm.facetresmm,
        sm.geomdeltamm,
        -- Determine if mesh is high-fidelity based on Knowledge #13
        CASE 
            WHEN (sm.facetfaces / (sm.facetverts * POWER(sm.facetresmm, 2))) * 1000 > 5.0 
                 AND sm.facetresmm < 1.0 
                 AND sm.geomdeltamm < 0.5 THEN TRUE
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS is_high_fidelity
    FROM scanmesh sm
    WHERE sm.facetverts > 0 AND sm.facetfaces > 0 -- Avoid division by zero
)

-- Step 2: Aggregate mesh quality metrics by site and identify sites with high-fidelity meshes
SELECT 
    s.zoneregistry AS site_code,
    s.zonelabel AS site_name,
    COUNT(ma.mesh_id) AS total_meshes,
    -- Count high-fidelity meshes
    SUM(CASE WHEN ma.is_high_fidelity THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_fidelity_count,
    -- Calculate percentage of high-fidelity meshes
    ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN ma.is_high_fidelity THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::numeric / 
           NULLIF(COUNT(ma.mesh_id), 0) * 100), 2) AS high_fidelity_percentage,
    -- Calculate average MCR, resolution, and geometric accuracy
    ROUND(AVG(ma.mcr)::numeric, 2) AS avg_mcr,
    ROUND(AVG(ma.facetresmm)::numeric, 2) AS avg_mesh_resolution_mm,
    ROUND(AVG(ma.geomdeltamm)::numeric, 2) AS avg_geometric_accuracy_mm,
    -- Determine site's mesh quality classification
    CASE 
        WHEN COUNT(ma.mesh_id) = 0 THEN 'No Mesh Data'
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN ma.is_high_fidelity THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Has High-Fidelity Meshes'
        ELSE 'Standard Mesh Quality'
    END AS mesh_quality_classification
FROM sites s
LEFT JOIN mesh_analysis ma ON s.zoneregistry = ma.site_code
GROUP BY s.zoneregistry, s.zonelabel
ORDER BY high_fidelity_percentage DESC, high_fidelity_count DESC;

question: To analyze digital engagement trends, please group customers into quarterly cohorts based on their tenure and identify Digital First Customers. For each combination of cohort quarter with whether they are Digital First Customers ('true' or 'false'), show the cohort quarter, bool value, the cohort size, the average Customer Engagement Score (CES), the percentage of the cohort with high engagement, and the percentage of Digital First Customers with high engagement.

List the top 10 high-risk data flows, showing each flow's ID, Risk Exposure Score, and Data Sensitivity Index, include all flows, even if risk or profile data is missing. Sort by Data Sensitivity Index from highest to lowest, rounding scores to two decimal places.
gold_sql:
WITH HighRiskFlows AS (
    SELECT 
        df.RecordRegistry, 
        COALESCE(rm.RiskAssess / NULLIF(rm.CtrlEff, 0), 0) AS res, 
        COALESCE(dp.VolGB, 0) * 
            CASE 
                WHEN dp.DataSense = 'High' THEN 3 
                WHEN dp.DataSense = 'Medium' THEN 2 
                ELSE 1 
            END AS dsi
    FROM DataFlow df
    LEFT JOIN RiskManagement rm 
        ON df.RecordRegistry = rm.FlowLink
    LEFT JOIN DataProfile dp 
        ON df.RecordRegistry = dp.FlowSign
    WHERE COALESCE(rm.RiskAssess / NULLIF(rm.CtrlEff, 0), 0) > 0.7 
        AND COALESCE(dp.VolGB, 0) * 
            CASE 
                WHEN dp.DataSense = 'High' THEN 3 
                WHEN dp.DataSense = 'Medium' THEN 2 
                ELSE 1 
            END > 100
),
RankedFlows AS (
    SELECT 
        RecordRegistry, 
        res, 
        dsi, 
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY dsi DESC) AS volume_rank
    FROM HighRiskFlows
)
SELECT 
    RecordRegistry, 
    ROUND(res::numeric, 2) AS risk_exposure_score, 
    ROUND(dsi::numeric, 2) AS data_sensitivity_index
FROM RankedFlows
WHERE volume_rank <= 10
ORDER BY volume_rank
LIMIT 10;

question: Calculate the Position Value at Risk (PVaR) for the top 5 positions, using their notional value from risk and margin data and the single latest market volatility reading. Show me the risk and margin pivot, the position's notional value, the volatility measure used, and the calculated PVaR.
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Compute the Position Value at Risk for a position using riskandmargin and market volatility.
Step 1: From riskandmargin, extract "possum" from the nested JSON (position.possum).
Step 2: Get the latest "volmeter" from marketstats (volatility measure).
Step 3: Compute PVaR = possum * volmeter * 0.01.
Advanced Functions Used: JSONB extraction, CROSS JOIN, Common Table Expression.
KB Knowledge Used: "Position Value at Risk (PVaR)" (id: 2).
*/
WITH position AS (
  SELECT 
    riskandmarginpivot,
    (risk_margin_profile->'position'->>'possum')::numeric AS possum
  FROM riskandmargin
  ORDER BY riskandmarginpivot DESC
  LIMIT 5  -- limit considered for illustration; in production, you might process many rows
),
vol AS (
  SELECT volmeter::numeric
  FROM marketstats
  ORDER BY marketstatsmark DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
  p.riskandmarginpivot,
  p.possum,
  vol.volmeter,
  (p.possum * vol.volmeter * 0.01) AS PVaR
FROM position p
CROSS JOIN vol;

question: Identify all Suspicious Transaction Patterns in our cybermarket database and list their details. Display the transaction ID, payment method, payment amount, escrow status, escrow hours, routing complexity, and calculate their Transaction Anomaly Score. Rank results by highest transaction anomaly scores first.
gold_sql:
-- Identify Suspicious Transaction Patterns based on knowledge ID 22, ID 12
-- Uses CASE expressions for paymethod evaluation

WITH market_escrow_rates AS (
    SELECT 
        mktregistry,
        esccomprate
    FROM 
        markets
)
SELECT 
    t.txregistry,
    t.paymethod,
    t.payamtusd,
    t.escrowused,
    t.escrowhrs,
    t.routecomplexity,
    -- Calculate Transaction Anomaly Score (Knowledge ID 12)
    (t.payamtusd/1000 * t.txfinishhrs/24 * 
     (1 + t.escrowhrs::float/100) * 
     (1 - mer.esccomprate/100)) AS transaction_anomaly_score
FROM 
    transactions t
JOIN 
    market_escrow_rates mer ON t.mktref = mer.mktregistry
WHERE 
    (t.payamtusd/1000 * t.txfinishhrs/24 * 
     (1 + t.escrowhrs::float/100) * 
     (1 - mer.esccomprate/100)) > 75
    AND t.paymethod = 'Crypto_B'
    AND (t.escrowused = 'No' OR t.escrowhrs < 24)
    AND t.routecomplexity = 'Complex'
ORDER BY 
    transaction_anomaly_score DESC;

question: Could you calculate the Public Health Resilience Score for all disaster areas and identify which ones are facing a Public Health Emergency? -- Intent: Calculate Public Health Resilience Score (PHRS) for disaster areas
-- Uses KB ID 17: Public Health Resilience Score (PHRS), ID 26
-- Advanced Functions: Weighted calculations, conditional classification

SELECT

    d.distregistry,

question: Find all potential Dormant Bots. Show account IDs, Bot Behavior Index scores, and classify them into risk levels: 'High' (BBI > 0.9), 'Moderate ' (0.3 < BBI <= 0.9), and 'Low Risk' (BBI <= 0.3). Only include accounts with BBI > 0.2, limit to top 100 highest-risk accounts. Make sure to include all dormant accounts, even if some detection or messaging data is not available.
gold_sql:
WITH bbi_calc AS (
    -- Step 1: Calculate Bot Behavior Index (BBI) for dormant accounts.
    -- Starts with account table to ensure dormant accounts are included, normalizes botlikscore.
    SELECT 
        a.accindex AS macntref,
        a.acctident,
        (0.4 * COALESCE((sd.detection_score_profile -> 'behavior_scores' ->> 'botlikscore')::numeric / 100, 0) + 
         0.3 * COALESCE((sd.detection_score_profile -> 'behavior_scores' ->> 'autobehavscore')::numeric, 0) + 
         0.3 * (1 - COALESCE(ma.convnatval, 0))) AS bbi_score
    FROM account a
    LEFT JOIN moderationaction m ON a.accindex = m.macntref
    LEFT JOIN securitydetection sd ON m.masedetref = sd.secdetkey
    LEFT JOIN messaginganalysis ma ON m.macntref = ma.msgcntref
    WHERE a.acctstatus = 'Dormant'
)
-- Step 2: Filter dormant accounts with BBI and assign risk category.
SELECT 
    bc.acctident,
    bc.bbi_score,
    CASE 
        WHEN bc.bbi_score > 0.9 THEN 'High'
        WHEN bc.bbi_score > 0.3 THEN 'Moderate '
        ELSE 'Low Risk'
    END AS risk_category
FROM bbi_calc bc
WHERE bc.bbi_score > 0.2  -- Lowered threshold for normalized BBI
ORDER BY bc.bbi_score DESC
LIMIT 100

question: Analyze wireless and bluetooth devices' Battery Efficiency Ratio and classify them according to the Battery Efficiency Classification. Please display manufacturer name, model, battery life (hours), battery capacity (mAh), active power consumption (mW), Battery Efficiency Ratio (rounded to 2 decimal places), and corresponding efficiency classification. Also calculate the efficiency percentile ranking within each manufacturer. All calculated values should be rounded to 2 decimal places. Sort results by Battery Efficiency Ratio from highest to lowest.
gold_sql:
/*
Analysis Goal: Analyze wireless devices based on Battery Efficiency Ratio (BER)
Knowledge Used: ID 1 - Battery Efficiency Ratio ID 50
Advanced Features: Window functions, conditional aggregation, string operations
*/

-- Step 1: Calculate Battery Efficiency Ratio (BER) for each wireless device
WITH ber_calc AS (
    SELECT 
        d.devregistry,
        d.makername,
        d.modnum,
        t.battlifeh,
        t.battcapmah,
        d.pwractmw,
        -- Calculate BER according to formula from knowledge ID 1
        (t.battlifeh * t.battcapmah) / (d.pwractmw * 10.0) AS ber
    FROM deviceidentity d
    JOIN testsessions t ON d.devsessionref = t.sessionregistry
    WHERE d.conntype LIKE '%Wireless%' OR d.conntype LIKE '%Bluetooth%'
)
-- Step 2: Analyze devices based on BER and categorize their efficiency
SELECT 
    makername AS manufacturer,
    modnum AS model,
    battlifeh AS battery_life_hours,
    battcapmah AS battery_capacity_mah,
    pwractmw AS active_power_draw_mw,
    ROUND(ber, 2) AS battery_efficiency_ratio,
    -- Categorize devices based on BER value
    CASE 
        WHEN ber > 7.5 THEN 'Excellent Efficiency'
        WHEN ber BETWEEN 5.0 AND 7.5 THEN 'Good Efficiency'
        WHEN ber BETWEEN 2.5 AND 4.9 THEN 'Average Efficiency'
        ELSE 'Poor Efficiency'
    END AS efficiency_category,
    -- Calculate percentile ranking within each manufacturer
    PERCENT_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY makername ORDER BY ber) AS efficiency_percentile
FROM ber_calc
ORDER BY ber DESC;

question: First, identify all traders who qualify as High-Risk Manipulator Candidates. Then, for this specific group of traders, calculate the average Unique Pattern Deviation Ratio based on their transaction history. Please provide only this single average value, rounded to two decimal places.
gold_sql:
-- SQL Intent: Calculate the average Unique Pattern Deviation Ratio (UPDR) specifically for traders identified as High-Risk Manipulator Candidates.
WITH TraderBaseMetrics AS (
    -- Step 1: Calculate DTR and TLE for KB ID 10.
    SELECT
        t.tradereg,
        t.voldaily / NULLIF(t.acctbal, 0) AS dtr,
        (t.trading_performance -> 'risklevel' ->> 'levratio')::numeric AS tle,
        (t.trading_performance -> 'risklevel' ->> 'risklevel') AS risk_level_text
    FROM trader t
), HighRiskTraders AS (
    -- Step 2: Identify High-Risk traders based on KB ID 10.
    SELECT tradereg FROM TraderBaseMetrics
    WHERE tle > 5.0 AND risk_level_text = 'Aggressive' OR dtr > 0.5
), ManipulationPatternTraders AS (
    -- Step 3: Identify traders linked to Layering/Spoofing patterns based on KB ID 12. Requires joining transactionrecord and calculating OMI (KB ID 1).
    SELECT DISTINCT
        tr.trdref AS tradereg
    FROM transactionrecord tr
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL ( -- Calculate OMI per transaction
        SELECT tr.modfreq / NULLIF(1 - tr.cancelpct, 0) AS omi
    ) AS omi_calc ON tr.cancelpct < 1
    WHERE
        (tr.risk_indicators ->> 'layerind') = 'Confirmed' -- KB ID 12, KB ID 31 context
        OR ( (tr.risk_indicators ->> 'spoofprob')::numeric > 0.75 -- KB ID 12, KB ID 32 context
             AND COALESCE(omi_calc.omi, 0) > 1.0 ) -- KB ID 12, KB ID 1
), HighRiskManipulators AS (
    -- Step 4: Combine High-Risk and Manipulation Pattern traders to identify High-Risk Manipulator Candidates (KB ID 60).
    SELECT hrt.tradereg FROM HighRiskTraders hrt
    INTERSECT
    SELECT mpt.tradereg FROM ManipulationPatternTraders mpt
), AdvancedBehaviorMetrics AS (
    -- Step 5: Calculate PAS and retrieve patsim for UPDR calculation (KB IDs 4, 28), joining relevant tables.
    SELECT
        tr.trdref AS tradereg,
        AVG(ABS(ab.patsim - ab.peercorr)) AS avg_pas, -- KB ID 4
        AVG(ab.patsim) AS avg_patsim -- Needed for UPDR, context KB ID 28
    FROM advancedbehavior ab
    JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
    GROUP BY tr.trdref
)
-- Step 6: Final Calculation - Calculate UPDR (KB ID 52) for High-Risk Manipulators and find the average.
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(abm.avg_pas / GREATEST(0.01, abm.avg_patsim)), 2) AS average_updr_for_high_risk_manipulators -- KB ID 52
FROM
    AdvancedBehaviorMetrics abm
WHERE
    abm.tradereg IN (SELECT tradereg FROM HighRiskManipulators) LIMIT 100

question: I want to identify which primary diagnoses are associated with the highest Crisis Intervention Frequency (CIF) across all patients. For each diagnosis, list the diagnosis name, the number of patients with that diagnosis, and the CIF value, rounded to two decimal places. Sort the results by CIF in descending order and limit to the top 100 diagnoses.
gold_sql:
WITH PatientDiagnosis AS (
    -- Step 1: Get the primary diagnosis for each patient from their most recent assessment.
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (ab.patownerref)
        ab.patownerref AS patkey,
        asd.primdx
    FROM assessmentbasics ab
    JOIN assessmentsocialanddiagnosis asd ON ab.abkey = asd.asdkey
    JOIN encounters e ON ab.abkey = e.abref
    WHERE asd.primdx IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY ab.patownerref, e.timemark DESC
), PatientCrisisInterventions AS (
    -- Step 2: Calculate the total crisis interventions per patient across all their treatment records.
    SELECT
        e.patref AS patkey,
        SUM(COALESCE(tb.crisisint, 0)) AS total_crisisint
    FROM treatmentbasics tb
    JOIN encounters e ON tb.encref = e.enckey
    GROUP BY e.patref
), PatientCount AS (
    -- Step 3: Count the number of patients for CIF denominator.
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patkey) AS total_patients FROM patients
)
-- Final Step: Calculate CIF per diagnosis group.
SELECT
    pd.primdx,
    COUNT(DISTINCT pci.patkey) AS num_patients_with_dx,
    ROUND(SUM(pci.total_crisisint) / pc.total_patients, 2) AS cif_per_diagnosis
FROM PatientDiagnosis pd
JOIN PatientCrisisInterventions pci ON pd.patkey = pci.patkey
CROSS JOIN PatientCount pc
GROUP BY pd.primdx, pc.total_patients
ORDER BY cif_per_diagnosis DESC
LIMIT 100

question: I want to see which historical periods have adequate conservation resources and which might be facing a Conservation Budget Crisis. For each dynasty, show the dynasty name, their total conservation priority index, the count of artifacts with adequate funding, the count with insufficient funding, the calculated CBE valuea, and a budget status that indicates 'Budget Crisis' if the dynasty meets the defined Conservation Budget Crisis criteria, and 'Within Budget' otherwise. Besides, please include a summary row for all dynasties combined labeled as 'ALL DYNASTIES'.
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Calculate Conservation Budget Efficiency (KB #8) by department.
Advanced features: Advanced aggregation with FILTER, ROLLUP
*/
WITH artifact_cpi AS (
    -- Step 1: Calculate CPI for each artifact (KB #0)
    SELECT 
        a.ArtRegistry,
        a.ArtName,
        a.ArtDynasty,
        ((r.HistSignRating + r.ResearchValRating + r.CultScore) * 
         CASE a.ConserveStatus
             WHEN 'Excellent' THEN 9  -- 10-1
             WHEN 'Good' THEN 7       -- 10-3
             WHEN 'Fair' THEN 5       -- 10-5
             WHEN 'Poor' THEN 3       -- 10-7
             WHEN 'Critical' THEN 0   -- 10-10
         END) / 30.0 AS CPI
    FROM ArtifactsCore a
    JOIN ArtifactRatings r ON a.ArtRegistry = r.ArtRef
),
budget_allocation AS (
    -- Step 2: Get budget allocation data
    SELECT 
        ArtRefMaintained AS ArtRegistry,
        SUM(CASE WHEN BudgetAllocStatus = 'Adequate' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS adequate_budget,
        SUM(CASE WHEN BudgetAllocStatus = 'Insufficient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS insufficient_budget,
        COUNT(*) AS total_records
    FROM ConservationAndMaintenance
    GROUP BY ArtRefMaintained
)
-- Step 3: Calculate CBE by dynasty using formula from KB #8
SELECT 
    COALESCE(a.ArtDynasty, 'ALL DYNASTIES') AS dynasty,
    COUNT(a.ArtRegistry) AS artifact_count,
    SUM(c.CPI) AS total_cpi,
    SUM(b.adequate_budget) AS artifacts_with_adequate_budget,
    SUM(b.insufficient_budget) AS artifacts_with_insufficient_budget,
    -- Calculate CBE: sum of (CPI * budget ratio) / count
    SUM(c.CPI * (b.adequate_budget::float / NULLIF(b.total_records, 0))) / 
    NULLIF(COUNT(a.ArtRegistry), 0) AS CBE,
    -- Step 4: Flag if dynasty has Conservation Budget Crisis (KB #16)
    CASE 
        WHEN SUM(c.CPI * (b.adequate_budget::float / NULLIF(b.total_records, 0))) / 
             NULLIF(COUNT(a.ArtRegistry), 0) < 0.5
             AND SUM(CASE WHEN a.ConserveStatus = 'Critical' AND b.insufficient_budget > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
        THEN 'Budget Crisis'
        ELSE 'Within Budget'
    END AS budget_status
FROM artifact_cpi c
JOIN ArtifactsCore a ON c.ArtRegistry = a.ArtRegistry
LEFT JOIN budget_allocation b ON c.ArtRegistry = b.ArtRegistry
GROUP BY ROLLUP(a.ArtDynasty);

question: Generate a report showing article engagement metrics grouped by category. For each article, calculate both the Article Quality Index (AQI) and Article Readability Score (ARS), then output the article category name with a JSON array containing each article's ID, category, calculated AQI score and ARS score (field names are 'artkey', 'catlabel', 'aqi', and 'ars').
gold_sql:
WITH article_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        artkey,
        catlabel,
        (qualscore + freshscore + sentscore - contrscore) / 3.0 AS aqi,
        -- difficulty weight w (KB 56)
        CASE difflevel
             WHEN 'Basic'        THEN 1.0
             WHEN 'Intermediate' THEN 1.5
             WHEN 'Advanced'     THEN 2.0
             ELSE 1.2
        END                                 AS diff_w,
        readsec,
        wordlen
    FROM articles
),
article_ars AS (
    SELECT
        artkey,
        catlabel,
        aqi,
        (readsec * LOG(wordlen)) / diff_w   AS ars            -- weighted ARS (KB 5)
    FROM article_metrics
)
SELECT 
    catlabel,
    json_agg(row_to_json(article_ars)) AS article_data
FROM article_ars
GROUP BY catlabel;

question: For each combination of station name and location type, I need to see station names, location types, average water quality indices, average WRMI scores (both rounded to 2 decimal places), count of systems with Water Conservation Requirement, water quality classification, and water resource management status. Sort by highest WRMI first, then by water quality.
gold_sql:
-- Intent: Analyze water resource management efficiency and its relationship to water quality
-- Uses knowledge IDs 7, 18, 25, 53 with conditional aggregation

-- Step 1: Calculate WRMI (Water Resource Management Index) for each water system
WITH wrmi_calc AS (
    SELECT 
        waw.watereqref,
        waw.waterlevelpercent * 
        (waw.waterqualityindex / 100) * 
        (1 - waw.wastetanklevelpercent / 100) AS wrmi
    FROM waterandwaste waw
)
-- Step 2: Analyze water resource management by station and water quality level
SELECT 
    l.stationname,
    l.locationtype,
    ROUND(AVG(waw.waterqualityindex)::numeric, 2) AS avg_water_quality_index,
    ROUND(AVG(wc.wrmi)::numeric, 2) AS avg_wrmi,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE wc.wrmi < 0.5) AS systems_needing_conservation,
    CASE 
        WHEN AVG(waw.waterqualityindex) >= 91 THEN 'High-Quality'
        WHEN AVG(waw.waterqualityindex) >= 71 THEN 'Good'
        WHEN AVG(waw.waterqualityindex) >= 51 THEN 'Moderate'
        WHEN AVG(waw.waterqualityindex) >= 26 THEN 'Poor'
        ELSE 'Unsafe'
    END AS quality_classification,
    CASE 
        WHEN AVG(wc.wrmi) < 0.5 THEN 'Conservation Needed'
        WHEN AVG(wc.wrmi) < 0.7 THEN 'Monitoring Advised'
        ELSE 'Sustainable Management'
    END AS management_status
FROM waterandwaste waw
JOIN equipment e ON waw.watereqref = e.equipmentcode
JOIN location l ON e.equipmentcode = l.loceqref
JOIN wrmi_calc wc ON waw.watereqref = wc.watereqref
GROUP BY l.stationname, l.locationtype
ORDER BY avg_wrmi DESC, avg_water_quality_index DESC;

question: Show me how solar panel performance changes with age by calculating the Panel Performance Ratio (PPR) for different age groups. I want to see the panel age in years since installation, the average PPR and the number of panels of each age group. Sort the results from newest to oldest panels.
gold_sql:
/*
Intent: Calculate average PPR grouped by panel age in years
Knowledge: Panel Performance Ratio (ID:0)
Features: Date functions, GROUP BY
*/
SELECT 
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM AGE(CURRENT_DATE, pl.initdate)) AS panel_age_years,
    AVG(pe.measpoww / p.powratew * 100) AS avg_ppr,
    COUNT(*) AS panel_count
FROM panel p
JOIN plant pl ON p.hubregistry = pl.growregistry
JOIN performance pe ON p.panemark = pe.solmodref
GROUP BY panel_age_years
ORDER BY panel_age_years;
